finding: Forward dynamics is abbreviated to torque-to-motion without explicitly listing model and initial state.
handling: Questions make the omitted model/state assumptions explicit; no uniqueness from torque alone is asserted.

finding: The slide presents positive definiteness and hard-constraint encoding without delimiting degenerate mass distributions or actual implementation.
handling: Questions explicitly assume a nondegenerate solid for positive definiteness; mathematical nonnegativity and implementation-dependent enforcement are separated.

finding: p362 defines Ixy=∫xy dm and p361 uses −Ixy in the tensor; p368 writes Ixy,A=Ixy,C−mxc yc, which is instead the signed matrix-entry rule. p369 confirms this by inserting −mwl/4. p376 repeats both conventions together.
handling: Use Pxy for raw products and I12 for signed tensor entries. Derive Pxy,A=Pxy,C+mxc yc and I12,A=I12,C−mxc yc. Preserve the slide notation conflict explicitly.

finding: The hollow-cylinder row mR² omits the thin-wall assumption; the plate row only says axis through center, omitting normal-to-plane direction.
handling: State thin shell and central normal axis explicitly. Derive the plate row from the box limit, and do not extend mR² to arbitrary wall thickness.

finding: The statements about smaller motors and COM stability across all configurations are unconditional in wording.
handling: Questions treat inertia reduction as a geometric consequence under stated assumptions and motor/COM benefits as design goals requiring load, motion and configuration checks.

finding: Inertia matching is called a universal efficiency maximum without a drive model or reflected-load convention; proximal mass is equated with better stability without conditions.
handling: Retain the matching criterion as an explicitly source-attributed heuristic. Require stated drive coordinates/objective and treat stability/agility statements as conditional design guidance.

finding: Strictly positive moments exclude ideal axis/point-supported distributions; trace invariance is stated for orientation changes, not translations. Practical measurement wording is not exclusive of the following CAD computation advice.
handling: Use nonnegative squared-distance derivation for degenerate cases, keep the origin fixed for orientation invariance, and distinguish measurement from calculation without treating either as forbidden.

finding: The slide calls ixx,iyy,izz principal moments and says products vanish if symmetric without stating axes.
handling: The shown tensor is diagonal, so its diagonal entries are principal. General tensor components need not be eigenvalues; symmetry must be relevant to the chosen origin and axes. The actual XML is preserved and parsed without repair.

supplementalImplementationReference.scope: Official ROS documentation confirms kg mass, the symmetric six-entry matrix, and the inertial-origin frame. This supports implementation convention checks, not replacement of the supplied lecture as course authority.

finding: The summary labels the coincident/zero-origin-acceleration expression as generalized but omits a0 from the general p359 equation.
handling: Explicit comparison questions preserve the omission. General numerical questions use p359; summary equation is restricted to a0=0.
